question.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=3xy+4x+6y-5{y}^{2}$, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,2).$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3xy+4x+6y-5{y}^{2})i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3xy+4x+6y-5{y}^{2})j \\  & =(3y+4)\,i+(3x+6-10y)\,j \\ ∇\,f(1,2) & =(3(2)+4)\,i+(3(1)+6-10(2))\,j \\  & =10\,i-11\,j \\  & =⟨10,-11⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,2)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨10,-11⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-2⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$
